item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
248
ABPZ20 KNHC 050508
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Fri Sep 4 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Karina, located several hundred miles east of the Hawaiian Islands,
on Hurricane Lowell, located several hundred miles south-southwest
of the Hawaiian Islands, and on Hurricane Marie, located several
hundred miles west-southwest of the southern tip of the Baja
California Peninsula.

Offshore of Southwestern Mexico:
An area of low pressure may develop well offshore of southwestern
Mexico early next week. Gradual development is possible, and a
tropical depression could form around the middle of next week while
it moves west-northwestward at 10 to 15 mph.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...60 percent.

$$
Forecaster Pierce/Gibbs

item.description:

000
WTPZ33 KNHC 050842

BULLETIN
Hurricane Marie Advisory Number  17
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP132026
200 AM PDT Sat Sep 05 2026
 
...MARIE WEAKENS A LITTLE AS IT MOVES NORTHWESTWARD...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 AM PDT...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...21.4N 119.7W
ABOUT 635 MI...1020 KM W OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...90 MPH...150 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 315 DEGREES AT 8 MPH...13 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...970 MB...28.65 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 AM PDT (0900 UTC), the center of Hurricane Marie was located
near latitude 21.4 North, longitude 119.7 West. Marie is moving
toward the northwest near 8 mph (13 km/h), and this general motion
is expected to continue for the next few days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are now near 90 mph (150 km/h) with higher
gusts.  A gradual weakening trend is expected to continue for the 
next several days.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 50 miles (85 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 205 miles
(335 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 970 mb (28.65 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Marie will continue to affect portions of
the coast of southwest Mexico, the Baja California Peninsula, and
Southern California for the next few days. These swells are likely
to cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please
consult products from your local weather office. A depiction of rip
current risk for the United States can be found at:
hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep3.shtml?ripCurrents
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 AM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Beven

item.title: Hurricane Marie Forecast Discussion Number 17
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM PDT Sat Sep 05 2026 
000
WTPZ43 KNHC 050843
TCDEP3
 
Hurricane Marie Discussion Number  17
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP132026
200 AM PDT Sat Sep 05 2026

Marie currently has a ragged banding eye in satellite imagery, 
which is open to the north due to a patch of dry air currently 
located to the north of the center. The various satellite intensity 
estimates have edged down just a little, and based on them the 
initial intensity is reduced to 80 kt.

The hurricane is now moving northwest or 315/7 kt. The cyclone 
should continue slowly northwestward for the next two to three days 
as it moves through a break in the subtropical ridge. After 72 h, 
Marie is forecast to encounter a large mid- to upper-level trough 
west of California. As that happens, the cyclone is likely to 
become decoupled vertically, with the low-level part of the 
circulation turning north-northwestward. The new track forecast is 
in best agreement with the HFIP Corrected Consensus model and is 
similar to the previous forecast. As in the previous advisory, it 
should be noted that model spread is quite large beyond 2 to 3 days.
 
For the first 24-36 h, Marie will be over seas surface temperatures 
of 26-27C and in a light vertical shear environment. During this 
time, dry air entrainment is forecast to cause a slow weakening. 
The weakening rate should increase after 36 h as the cyclone moves 
over colder water, and after 72 h strong shear associated with the 
aforementioned trough should become the final factor in causing the 
associated convection to dissipate. The new intensity forecast has 
a few tweaks to better follow the overall trend of the guidance, 
and it calls for the system to weaken until it degenerates to a 
remnant low around 120 h.
